heading: Subsequence window with 1D DP
body:
**Don't check every substring** (O(m³)). Track where each partial match **started**.

`dp[j]` = starting index in `s1` from which we can form `s2[0..j]` ending at current position.

When `s1[i] == s2[j]`:
- `j==0`: new window starts at `i`
- `j>0`: inherit start from `dp[j-1]`

heading: Why iterate backwards?
body:
**Iterate `j` from `n-1` down to `0`** to avoid overwriting `dp[j-1]` before using it.

Since `dp[j] = dp[j-1]` when matching, forward iteration would clobber the value you need next.

label: Crux · Python

q: Why do we iterate through s2 in reverse order (j from n-1 to 0) when updating the dp array?
options: To avoid overwriting dp[j-1] before using it for dp[j]
To match the subsequence from right to left
To ensure we find the leftmost window first
explain: Since dp[j] depends on dp[j-1], iterating forwards would overwrite dp[j-1] before we use it to update dp[j].
